Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report highlights an incorrect value in the `Base32.HEX_DECODE_TABLE` at line 99. The array contains the value 32 at an index where it should not, specifically in the range corresponding to characters 'O' through 'V'. This incorrect value disallows using 'W' as padding with the hex table format. The failing test case `testCodec200()` tries to instantiate a Base32 codec with hex mode set to true and padding byte 'W'. Because of the wrong value (32) in the decode table where 'W' padding should be allowed, this test fails. The constructor `Base32(boolean useHex, byte pad)` passes the hex usage and padding byte 'W', but due to the corrupted decode table, the decoder will not correctly recognize the padding byte. This corroborates the bug report summary that `HEX_DECODE_TABLE` contains an invalid entry (32) which should be removed or fixed to allow proper decoding and padding with 'W'. The root cause is the corrupted decode table at line 99, which incorrectly includes the value 32.

This diagnosis links the failing test (using hex mode and pad 'W'), the bug report (wrong value 32 in hex decode table), and the relevant source code snippet showing the corrupted decode table.
